islamicFacts: The Hijri calendar begins with the Prophet's ﷺ migration from Makkah to Madinah.
Ramadan is the ninth month of the Hijri calendar.
The sacred months are: Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab.
Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months and is sought in the last ten days of Ramadan.
Friday is the best day of the week for Muslims.
Fasting on the Day of Arafah expiates the sins of two years, by Allah's will, for non-pilgrims.
The Day of Ashura is a blessed day, and fasting on it is recommended.
Zakat, Fasting, and Hajj are connected to the Hijri calendar.
Sighting the crescent moon is a Sunnah associated with the beginning of Hijri months.
Islamic holidays are determined by the Hijri calendar, not the Gregorian.
